title: Shastri Urges India to Spare Bumrah, Backs Shami Recall and Bhuvneshwar Return
excerpt: The former head coach says Bumrah should be preserved for Tests until the 2027 ODI World Cup, Shami has "done enough" for a recall, and Bhuvneshwar's experience is a no-brainer for New Zealand conditions.
body:
• Former India coach Ravi Shastri says Jasprit Bumrah should not play all three formats before the 2027 ODI World Cup, and should be preserved mainly for Test cricket with only sporadic ODI and T20I appearances.
  • Shastri welcomed Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return to the T20I squad for the New Zealand tour, calling the swing bowler's experience and IPL form a "no-brainer" for New Zealand conditions.
  • He also backed Mohammed Shami for a Test and ODI recall: Shami, out since the 2025 Champions Trophy, took 37 wickets in seven Ranji Trophy matches for Bengal last season and seven wickets in three Duleep Trophy matches.
  • Bumrah has been recalled to the Test squad for New Zealand but will sit out the five ODIs and five T20Is that precede the two Tests; India begin the tour on October 22.

India should keep Jasprit Bumrah fresh for next year's ODI World Cup by selecting him mainly for Test cricket and using the pace spearhead sparingly in the other formats, former head coach Ravi Shastri has said, in comments reported by Reuters and Indian media on Sunday. Bumrah has been recalled to India's Test squad for the two-match series in New Zealand, but will not play the five ODIs and five T20Is that precede the Tests.

"I don't think he should play all three formats till the ODI World Cup. He should play Test cricket and should play sporadically between one-day internationals and T20 cricket. I would rather preserve him for the Test matches."

— Ravi Shastri, former India head coach

An injury record that forces the question

Bumrah's career has been repeatedly disrupted by injury. The 32-year-old underwent back surgery in 2023, was ruled out of the two-Test series against Sri Lanka in August with a left knee injury, and returned to T20 action at the Asian Games, where he helped India win gold. Shastri, who coached India from 2017 to 2021, argued that with the 2027 World Cup — to be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2 to November 21 — as the horizon, every Bumrah appearance outside Tests is a calculated risk.

The case for Shami

Shastri was equally direct about the bowler who is not in any of the squads. Mohammed Shami has not played for India since the 2025 Champions Trophy, where he took nine wickets; he remains India's highest wicket-taker in ODI World Cups with 55. Since then he has rebuilt his case in domestic cricket, taking seven wickets in three Duleep Trophy matches at 26.57 as East Zone won the title, and 37 wickets in seven matches for Bengal in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, Mint noted, though his IPL returns were modest. "He's done enough with both red and white balls to be recalled to the Test and ODI sides," Shastri said.

Experience for New Zealand conditions

The third veteran in Shastri's assessment is already back. Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return to the T20I squad drew his warmest praise. "There is no substitute for experience," Shastri told The Times of India. "When you have a bowler of Bhuvneshwar's quality and experience, it's a no-brainer. With the form he showed in the IPL and his years with India, he'll be ideal for New Zealand conditions." The six-week tour, which opens on October 22 with five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests, is India's last major away assignment before a home summer that ends with a five-Test series against Australia in February.

What it means for India's planning

Shastri framed the tour as a benchmark for where Indian cricket is heading, with New Zealand conditions offering a preview of what India may face in South Africa at the World Cup. The harder arithmetic is in the World Test Championship, where he said India probably need to win around 90% of their remaining games — including both Tests in New Zealand and at least four of five against Australia — to reach the final. His prescription adds up to a clear selection philosophy for the season: spend Bumrah only where he is irreplaceable, and stop leaving proven seamers at home.
